metadata.notes: agent_supports: yes (`muse resume <uuid>` live-confirmed to reopen and APPEND to the SAME session.jsonl at the SAME directory path — no new session ever minted); daemon_capability: full; driver_capability: gap:resume (resume is not_implemented in driver-interactive.sh)

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full; driver_capability: gap:resume

## agent — yes

`muse --help` declares a top-level `resume` subcommand ("Resume a previous session (--last or <session-uuid>)"); `muse resume --help` documents `muse resume <session-uuid>` and `muse resume --last` ("Resume the most recent session in this workspace").

**Live-confirmed, not just doc-read.** I drove muse in a throwaway directory (`/tmp/muse-resume-probe`, never inside the repo) via `tmux send-keys`/`capture-pane`: launched `muse --provider echo`, sent one prompt, and captured the session directory it created — `~/.local/share/muse/sessions/2026/09/14/01a09f25-0880-7763-9990-5b13cfddca8a/` (72 lines in session.jsonl after turn 1). Sent `/exit`; the tmux server died with it (muse's own `session.end` record shows `exit_reason:"clean"`, and lsof on `.session.lock` went from an open fd to none — matches format-spec §1's documented clean-exit signal). Then ran `muse resume 01a09f25-0880-7763-9990-5b13cfddca8a --provider echo` in the SAME cwd: the TUI printed **`resumed session 01a09f25-0880-7763-9990-5b13cfddca8a`** and replayed the prior turn in-place. `.session.lock` was rewritten with the NEW process's pid (confirmed against `ps aux`). Sent a second prompt; the turn completed normally. Throughout, `session.jsonl` at the ORIGINAL path grew monotonically (72 → 76 → 131 lines) — **no second directory or file was ever created anywhere under `~/.local/share/muse/sessions/`.** The record stream itself makes the mechanism explicit: line 71 `session.end`(`exit_reason:clean`) closes lifetime 1; line 73 `session.opened.observed`; line 74 a distinct `session.resumed` record (`payload.kind:"session_resumed"`) — muse's own native marker for exactly this event; line 91 is lifetime 2's `runtime.session`/`run`/`started`.

This answers the cell-specific question directly: resume reuses the SAME session id (the directory basename) and appends to the existing `session.jsonl` — it does NOT mint a fresh file, and it does NOT read from `~/.local/share/muse/sessions/.msp-view-v1/<uuid>/` as a resume data source. I inspected that directory too (`HEAD.json`, `journal-*.bin`, `index-*.bin`, `snapshot-*.json`): `HEAD.json`'s `session_id` field matches its parent's directory basename 1:1, and its `source_through.sequence` field points BACK into `session.jsonl`'s own record sequence — this is a derived/materialized VIEW cache built FROM session.jsonl (for muse's own resume/rewind UI), not an alternate source of truth, and the adapter never reads it (`core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/adapter.go`'s permission `Detail` enumerates every file the adapter touches — `.session.lock`, `model-catalog/*`, `session.jsonl` — `.msp-view-v1` is absent). So the two outcomes the cell-specific pointer asked to distinguish resolve unambiguously in favor of "appends to the existing session.jsonl," with `.msp-view-v1` confirmed as an irrelevant, non-authoritative side cache.

## daemon — full

The adapter's `Source` is `agent.FilesUnderRoot` keyed on the session directory tree, with `SessionIDFromPath` deriving the id from the directory basename (`agent.go`). Because resume reopens the EXACT SAME file at the EXACT SAME path, no new session row can ever be minted by the birth path — the only question is whether the daemon correctly treats a late-arriving write on an already-known-but-now-orphaned session_id as "the same session coming back" rather than dropping it or (worse) never noticing it. I traced this through the generic (adapter-agnostic) session lifecycle code, not just the adapter:

- **Process exit deletes the row, not just marks it terminal.** `PIDManager.HandleProcessExit` (`core/application/services/pid_manager.go:467-484`) unconditionally calls `deleteWithChildren` when a session's PID is found dead — the doc comment there (lines 448-462) explains this is deliberate post-#1860 (a prior "retain as error" branch was removed because irrlicht is never the agent's parent and can't distinguish a crash from a clean exit). So after `/exit`, the daemon's session ROW is gone, not merely idle.
- **Re-attachment is write-triggered, not polling, and re-admits under the IDENTICAL session_id.** The fswatcher tracks last-known size per PATH independent of the domain repo (`core/adapters/inbound/agents/fswatcher/watcher.go`'s `handleTranscriptWrite`), so a write to an already-seen path always surfaces as activity. `SessionDetector.processActivity` (`core/application/services/session_detector_activity.go:622-686`) then loads the (now-deleted) row, finds nothing, and checks a tombstone: `deletedSessions` + a `deletedCooldown` of **10 seconds** (`session_detector.go`). If the write lands AFTER the cooldown and the file isn't stale, it clears the tombstone and falls through to `d.onNewSession(id, ev)` — which re-creates the row under the SAME session_id (deterministic from the transcript path) with a fresh `FirstSeen`, then kicks off `DiscoverPIDWithRetry` (`pid_manager.go`) to rebind the new PID. **If the write lands WITHIN the 10s cooldown, the function returns early and the write is silently dropped** — this is a real, load-bearing timing constraint on the RECIPE (see driver notes and caveats below), not a daemon defect.
- **No presession complexity is needed for this mechanism.** `agent.FilesUnderRoot` (`core/domain/agent/source.go`) has no presession concept at all — that machinery is driven by raw `Process.Match` scanning, which muse's adapter also declares (`CommandPattern`) but which plays no role here since the transcript already exists and activity is handled directly through `onNewSession`/`PIDForSession`, never through a `proc-<PID>` row. This is why muse (like pi, its structural sibling) needs no two-phase presession birth model for the SECOND lifetime the way codex/gemini-cli/hermes do.
- **PID rebinding on the second lifetime is precise.** `DiscoverPID` (`core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/pid.go`) asks `lsof` who holds THIS session's own `.session.lock` fd open — confirmed live: after the resume relaunch the lock file's stamped `pid=<N>` text changed from the exited process's pid to the new resume process's pid, matching `ps aux`'s `muse-bin-... resume 01a09f25... --provider echo` entry. This is a per-session lookup (not a name+cwd scan), so it can't misattribute across muse's documented `muse serve` one-PID-many-sessions shape either.
- **The re-admitted row starts at ready, not the prior terminal state.** `buildNewSessionState` sets `State: session.StateReady` unconditionally (`session_detector_activity.go:259`, doc comment: "All new sessions start as ready"). So the spec's "state ready initially [on resume]" and "ready → working on the first new turn" are both exactly what the generic machinery already produces.

This is the SAME generic mechanism already proven green on `pi`'s committed `session-resume` recording (`replaydata/agents/pi/scenarios/1-4_session-resume`) — pi is muse's closest structural sibling for this scenario: `FilesUnderRoot`, no presession, PID rediscovery via a per-session lookup rather than a name scan. Muse's own turn-boundary parsing (`runEventStarted`/`runEventTerminal` in `parser.go`) is unrelated to and unaffected by resume — it is the SAME mechanism basic-turn already exercises for both v1 and v2. The muse-native `session.opened.observed`/`session.resumed`/`session.end` records fall into the parser's default `Skip=true` branch (`parser.go`'s `route` function) — the daemon doesn't need to specially parse them because the generic process-exit/re-attach machinery above already reconstructs the correct observable arc from file presence and turn-boundary events alone.

## driver — gap:resume

`replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh` line 674: `resume) not_implemented resume || break ;;`, and `DRIVE_ELICITS` (line 167) is `"send slash wait_turn sleep exit_clean restart sigkill start_session session"` — `resume` is conspicuously absent. This is tooling work, not an observability limit: `step_restart` (line 527) already implements almost the whole shape for a FRESH session (kill tmux, allocate a new slot+cwd, relaunch) — porting `resume` is the same shape MINUS allocating a new slot (reuse the ACTIVE slot's existing `SES_UUID`/`SES_CWD`) and PLUS passing `resume "$uuid"` instead of no subcommand. The cell stays a real cell with a real recipe; `record` ports the step before driving, exactly as the hermes sibling cell documents for its own `gap:resume`.
caveats: PROVISIONAL on daemon EMISSION timing: this assess pass live-probed the TRANSCRIPT (muse's own session.jsonl) but did not run irrlichd against the probe, so the exact real-time shape of the resulting events.jsonl (event ordering, debounce coalescing) is not directly observed — it is derived from reading the generic session-lifecycle code cited above. `record` is what promotes this from provisional to settled, per the assess convention (hermes' sibling cell for this same scenario carries the identical caveat).

LOAD-BEARING RECIPE TIMING: the daemon's deletedSessions cooldown is 10s (core/application/services/session_detector_activity.go's processActivity — see body). A transcript write for this session_id arriving WITHIN 10s of the daemon detecting lifetime 1's process exit is silently dropped, not queued or retried — only a write landing after the cooldown re-admits the row under the same session_id. The recipe's resume step must sleep comfortably past 10s before the resumed turn's first write lands (the recipe below uses 12s) or the whole resumed turn is invisible to the daemon even though muse itself resumed correctly and would make the cell fail for a timing reason that has nothing to do with the behavior being tested.

`.msp-view-v1/<uuid>/` (HEAD.json, journal-*.bin, snapshot-*.json) is a derived view/rewind cache the adapter never reads (confirmed against adapter.go's enumerated permission Detail) — ruled out as a resume data source, not a candidate worth re-investigating.

The live probe used `--provider echo` (the deterministic test stub) and hit an echo-specific quirk on resume: `session ... does not record a usable model for provider echo; using the provider default model`. This is cosmetic to the echo stub, not a resume defect, but `record` should use the SAME real provider/model settings on both launches (matching muse's other committed cells, which pin `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` from real `--provider meta` runs) rather than `--provider echo`, to avoid the warning contaminating the recording.

Recipe records the single clean-exit-then-resume variant only, matching claudecode/pi/hermes' committed cells for this scenario. The scenario's second variant (multiple kill+resume cycles across many PID lifetimes) shares the same observability surface and would be a follow-up cell if regression coverage warrants it.

Vacuous-pass check: muse fires ambient reminder/goal-verify micro-agents on nearly every turn, each getting its own `ParentSessionID`-linked subagent directory indistinguishable from a real subagent at the generic event level (measured fact, wave-1 corpus). Every phase below is pinned `same_session_as:session_birth` for exactly this reason — an unpinned phase could silently match a companion reminder session's own ready/working arc instead of the primary session's, passing while proving nothing about resume specifically.

sources.note: `resume` top-level subcommand: "Resume a previous session (--last or <session-uuid>)"; `muse resume --help` documents `muse resume <session-uuid>` and `--last` ("Resume the most recent session in this workspace").

session 01a09f25-0880-7763-9990-5b13cfddca8a: launch -> turn 1 (72 lines) -> /exit (session.end exit_reason:clean, lock fd released) -> `muse resume 01a09f25... --provider echo` in the SAME cwd printed 'resumed session 01a09f25...', .session.lock rewritten with the new PID, session.jsonl grew to 131 lines at the SAME path across a second turn. No second session directory was ever created.
session_id field matches the parent directory basename; source_through.sequence points back into session.jsonl's own sequence — a derived view cache, not a resume data source.

Source: agent.FilesUnderRoot with SessionIDFromPath deriving the id from the session directory basename; the permission Detail enumerates every file read (.session.lock, model-catalog/*, session.jsonl) and .msp-view-v1 is absent from it.
DiscoverPID asks lsof who holds THIS session's own .session.lock fd open (not a name+cwd scan) — the lookup that rebinds a newly-launched resume PID to the existing session id.

route()'s default branch Skip=true's session.opened.observed/session.end (and, by the same catch-all, session.resumed) — the daemon derives the resumed arc from generic process-exit/re-attach + turn-boundary events, not from muse-native resume markers.
HandleProcessExit unconditionally deletes the session row on PID death (doc comment explains the post-#1860 removal of a prior 'retain as error' branch).

The 10s deletedSessions cooldown gate: a same-session-id write within 10s of deletion is dropped; after 10s it clears the tombstone and calls onNewSession, which re-creates the row under the SAME session_id at State=ready with a fresh FirstSeen.
agent.FilesUnderRoot has no presession field/concept — confirms muse needs no two-phase presession birth model for the resumed lifetime, unlike codex/gemini-cli/hermes.

pi's already-recorded (observed) session-resume cell: the closest structural sibling (FilesUnderRoot, no presession, per-session PID rediscovery) — the precedent this verdict leans on for daemon=full.
hermes' driver-gap:resume sibling cell for the SAME scenario — recipe/caveat shape (provisional-on-emission, scope_note for the single-variant recording) this assessment follows.
DRIVE_ELICITS omits resume; line 674 is `not_implemented resume`; step_restart (527) is the reference shape to specialize (reuse the ACTIVE slot instead of allocating a new one).

preconditions: muse CLI on PATH and authenticated (muse login or META_API_KEY) — confirmed installed at 1.2.1 on this machine
irrlichd is recording (--attach or isolated coexist mode)

drive-muse-interactive.sh must expose the `resume` step type (currently not_implemented at line 674, absent from DRIVE_ELICITS at line 167): port from step_restart (line 527), reusing the ACTIVE slot's existing SES_UUID/SES_CWD instead of allocating a new one, and relaunching `muse resume "${SES_UUID[$ACTIVE]}" --trust-workspace` (plus the same --model/--base-url MUSE_ARGS as the original launch) with `-c "${SES_CWD[$ACTIVE]}"` under a rotated tmux session name

LOAD-BEARING: the resume step's sleep before its relaunch settles/the resumed turn's first write must clear the daemon's 10s deletedSessions cooldown (session_detector_activity.go's processActivity) with margin, or the resumed activity is silently dropped by the daemon even though muse itself resumed correctly — the script below uses 12s

RECIPE CORRECTION (record, live-evidenced, 2026-09-15): the original script sent the post-resume turn immediately after `resume` with no intervening sleep -- unlike every other adapter's own committed session-resume recipe for this scenario (pi: resume,sleep 4,send; hermes: resume,sleep 6,send; codex: resume,sleep 4,send). A live recording with no gap showed the ENTIRE second turn complete and land on disk while the daemon's 10s deletedSessions cooldown (session_detector_activity.go) was still active; by the time the cooldown cleared and the row was re-admitted, the transcript already held a COMPLETE terminal record, so buildNewSessionState's unconditional State=ready meant the daemon never observed an intermediate working state -- v2_turn_start/v2_turn_end failed (6/8 phases). Confirmed directly against pi's own committed recording (replaydata/agents/pi/scenarios/1-4_session-resume), whose events.jsonl shows the SAME two-step shape working when a post-resume sleep is present: session reborn ready, then (after the sleep) a SEPARATE force-ready-to-working transition ~3-4s later from the actual send. A 6s sleep is inserted between resume and the post-resume send to match this established pattern.
setup: Driver captures SES_UUID/SES_CWD during turn 1's wait_turn via the existing resolve_transcript seam (driver-interactive.sh:319-355, the newest session.jsonl newer than the slot's marker) — muse assigns its own uuid at first-turn time and offers no --session-id flag to pre-select one, so the UUID is discovered, not generated.

The `resume` step reuses the SAME slot (no alloc_slot, no new N_SLOTS entry) — one session_id spans two PID lifetimes, matching hermes'/codex's resume step convention. Unlike `restart`, resolve_transcript's marker-bump-and-exclude-prior-file logic must NOT run for resume — the target is the SAME session.jsonl, not a new one.

Use the SAME --model/--provider settings on both the initial launch and the resume relaunch. A live probe found `muse resume <uuid> --provider echo` prints a resume-specific warning ('session ... does not record a usable model for provider echo; using the provider default model') — cosmetic to the echo test stub, but record should launch with the same real provider/model muse's other committed cells use rather than --provider echo, to keep the recording clean.

script.text: Reply with exactly the word: ok
Reply with exactly the word: again

verify: events.jsonl shows the session born ready shortly after launch (single-birth, no presession row needed — the session directory IS the row)
ready -> working -> ready for turn 1 on the session_id
a process_exited event on the session_id shortly after exit_clean's /exit (clean exit; .session.lock fd released, session.end exit_reason:clean on disk)

the SAME session_id shows activity again AFTER that process_exited — NOT a new session_id — this is the spec's 'Same session_id reappears (not a new session row)'; on disk, muse's own session.opened.observed + session.resumed records corroborate it (daemon-Skip=true bookkeeping, not required for the state signal itself)
ready -> working -> ready for turn 2 on the SAME session_id
final session state is ready; zero tool calls in either turn

on disk: exactly ONE session directory/file for this session_id throughout — session.jsonl grows monotonically across both lifetimes (live probe measured 72 -> 76 -> 131 lines), never a second directory under sessions/<Y>/<M>/<D>/
recipe.scope_note: Records the clean-exit-then-resume variant only, matching claudecode/pi/hermes' committed cells for this scenario. The scenario's second variant (multiple kill+resume cycles across many PID lifetimes) shares the same observability surface and can be a follow-up cell if regression coverage warrants it.
